claims.text: The as-cast (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy is a solid-solution alloy.
The unchanged alloy displays a large caloric response.
The unchanged alloy has poor mechanical integrity and is prone to cracking under load.
The proposed intervention is approximately 70% warm-to-cold rolling, beginning at 500–600 °C and finishing near room temperature, followed by annealing for 1–2 hours at 300–400 °C.
The specified rolling and annealing treatment will refine the alloy's microstructure.
The specified treatment will produce partial nanotwinning.
The treated alloy will remain predominantly single-phase and will not form detrimental new phases.
Controlled rolling and low-temperature annealing will introduce dislocation substructures and twin boundaries in this alloy.
Twin boundaries impede dislocation motion and thereby strengthen the treated alloy.
Multiple or nanoscale twins can enhance ductility while retaining high strength.
The treatment-induced dislocation and twin structures will reduce crack-initiation sites.
Grain refinement and partial nanotwinning will increase ductility and fracture toughness and reduce cracking relative to the as-cast alloy.
Retaining a single-phase matrix is important for preserving the alloy's caloric effects.
The treatment will preserve the original magnetocaloric performance without significant loss.
The treatment will preserve the original barocaloric performance without significant loss.
The proposed integrity and caloric benefits apply at magnetic fields up to approximately 2 T, hydrostatic pressures up to approximately 300 MPa, and temperatures from approximately 200 to 350 K.
Improper control of rolling and annealing could cause a phase transformation or loss of functional response.
The exact processing window for the optimal strength–caloric balance is uncertain, and extreme cycling may still produce microcracks.
